prs.title: Encode LSP messages directly instead of via MarshalJSON
prs.author: hood
prs.body:
Fixes #65371

`lsproto.Message` only had the old `[]byte`-returning `MarshalJSON`, so json/v2 got the already-encoded bytes back and validated + copied the whole payload again before writing it out 🫠. Switched it to `MarshalJSONTo`, so the wrapped message gets encoded straight into the encoder. Payload is identical, just a lot less work for big responses like completions, semantic tokens and diagnostics.

**Some raw numbers plus a real-world test on a reasonably-sized OSS project (`recharts`):**
| | `main` | this PR | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BenchmarkMarshalCompletionResponse` (2k items, n=10) | 1.934 ms ±7% | 1.273 ms ±1% | −34.2% (p=0.000) |
| B/op | 1243 KiB | 467 KiB | −62.5% |
| allocs/op | 37 | 16 | −57% |
| completion in `recharts` `Line.tsx` (531 KB) | 2.93 ms | 1.89 ms | −36% |

```sh
go -C ./tsc test -run '^$' -bench MarshalCompletionResponse -count 10 ./internal/lsp/lsproto
```

Tests:
- added `TestMarshalMessage`, which checks a wrapped `Message` encodes exactly like the message inside it (invalid UTF-8, HTML chars, null result, error response). It passes on `main` too, so it's really just pinning the output.
- diffed the output against `main` on the real 531 KB completion payload too, byte-identical.
- `npx hereby test`, `npx hereby lint` and `npx hereby check:format` all pass.

AI disclosure: I helped myself review and, most importantly, measured this with Claude Code. I've gone through everything it's added and I'll handle the review myself ofc.

prs.title: Collect garbage before writing allocation profiles
prs.author: jakebailey
prs.body:
The profile only shows stuff up to the last GC, which means that much of the time a lot can be missing from the profile. For example, doing `--pprofDir` on the webpack benchmark loses something like 50% of the samples!

Add the `GC` call where it should be; `SaveHeapProfile` already got this right.

prs.title: Go to a content-mapped file from its module specifier
prs.author: NullVoxPopuli
prs.body:
Fixes #64828

Go-to-definition on a module specifier now goes to the top of a content-mapped target file. Before, it returned nothing when the target was a content-mapped file.

## Problem

For a module specifier, the declaration is the target `SourceFile`. `createDefinitionLocations` maps the whole file's range, from the first token to the end of the file. The `IsSingleSegment` check then drops that range unless one segment covers all of it. A mapper can't fix this from its side.

Relative `import` specifiers were not affected, because they take the `getReferenceAtPosition` path. These were affected:

- `export ... from "./Card.vue"`
- non-relative specifiers, such as a `paths` alias: `import { title } from "@/Card.vue"`

## Fix

When the declaration is a `SourceFile` in a content-mapped file, `createDefinitionLocations` returns a zero-length location at the top of the original file. It does not map the file's range. This matches what the `getReferenceAtPosition` path already returns.

## Test

`contentMapperModuleSpecifierDefinition` uses two mappers. `.vue` goes through the component mapper, which emits several segments. `.foo` goes through the verbatim mapper, which emits one. The test runs go-to-definition on five specifiers:

- relative `import` of `.vue`
- `paths` alias `import` of `.vue` and of `.foo`
- `export ... from` of `.vue` and of `.foo`

On `main`, only the relative `import` returns a location. With this change, all five go to the target file at 0:0.

prs.title: Adjust folding range's end line only if closing bracket followed by non-trivia
prs.author: gabritto
prs.body:
Fixes #64235.

This PR roughly implements the algorithm described in #64235.

Basically before the PR, if the client had `lineOnly: true`, and the folding range ended with some kind of closing bracket, we'd recede the end line by one, so that the closing bracket is visible once the range is collapsed.
However, this behavior is not the one desired by many users (see https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/3352), who'd rather not see a single line with only a closing bracket. Since vscode is not planning on supporting `lineOnly: false` any time soon, this PR allows us to adopt the better behavior for TS: now we only recede the end line if there's some non-whitespace character in the same line as the closing bracket (and therefore it's likely relevant for the user to see that line).

I'm not sure however if we should indeed show a `};` in the case of:
```ts
if (blah) {
    ...
};
```
Also not sure if we should omit the closing bracket if there's a comment on that line, though maybe that's not very common.

I also took the liberty of changing the algorithm in the case of a content-mapped file.
If the TS file we're computing ranges for is generated by a content mapper, we can't be sure that absence of non-whitespace in the same line as a closing bracket in the TS file means there isn't any relevant information to show in the corresponding original line. prs.title: Keep nested JSDoc properties after a property with a missing name
prs.author: NullVoxPopuli
prs.body:
Fixes #65020

When a nested `@property` type does not parse, every nested property after it is lost. With this change they are kept, as they are in flat typedefs and in TS 6.

```js
/**
 * @typedef Sig
 * @property {object} Args
 * @property {string} Args.name
 * @property {function(string)=} Args.onSave
 * @property {((v: string) => void)=} Args.onCancel
 */
```

- Before: `keyof Sig['Args']` is `"name"`.
- After: `keyof Sig['Args']` is `"" | "name" | "onCancel"`. The `TS1005` on `function(` stays.

## Cause

The type parse stops at `(`, so the name of the `Args.onSave` tag is a missing identifier. `parseChildParameterOrPropertyTag` reads a plain identifier name as the start of a new top-level property, so it ended the `Args` type literal there. `Args.onSave` and `Args.onCancel` were then parsed at the typedef level.

The fix skips that check when the name is missing, so the tag stays in the nested literal. That gives the same `""` property that a flat typedef gets for the same tag.

## Test

`jsdocNestedPropertyTagInvalidType.ts` has a nested and a flat typedef with the same broken property, and `keyof` checks in a `.ts` file. Without the fix it reports `TS2322` and `TS2339` for `onCancel`.

`npx hereby test` passes with no other baseline changes. `hereby lint` and `hereby check:format` pass.

prs.title: Fix content mapper's virtual file module format
prs.author: andrewbranch
prs.body:
Fixes #65135

Also issues a diagnostic when the `extension` provided in a Transform response implies a module format that disagrees with the module format that will be assigned to the declaration file output. For example, if you respond to Transform as a `.mts` file, then either your package.json must have `"type": "module"` or your configured `outputExtensions` must map your custom file extension to a `.mjs` output. This is because the module format of a declaration file name like `App.d.svelte.ts` is always determined by the package.json, so it would create problems if that decision disagrees with what the virtual file claims to be.
